title: Progressive layout & stacking heuristics for Console cost/rollout dashboards
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and prototype a progressive/adaptive layout system for the Redwood Console pages that prioritize content and interaction on small viewports while preserving rich dashboard, rollout, and cost table/chart functionality on desktop. Work includes stacking heuristics for panels and cards, cross-browser fallbacks for canvas-based charts, modal stacking/focus behavior, and a responsive table strategy that supports large datasets without layout jank.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrating three key breakpoints (<=480px, 481–1024px, >1024px) for: cost overview, rollout detail, and a large-chart dashboard panel
Cross-browser QA checklist with pass/fail records for Chrome, Firefox, Safari (macOS and iOS), and Edge on Windows; documented fallback behavior for browsers missing advanced CSS features
Accessibility keyboard + focus tests for modal stacks and table pagination (no focus loss, screen reader friendly order)
Performance notes showing no >150ms layout shift on initial render for cost pages on 3G CPU throttled profile
Design handoff tokens and CSS guidance (containment, will-change, z-index rules, preferred overflow patterns) for eng implementation
decisions: Adopt a content-priority stacking model: primary content (chart/table) stays top in narrow viewports; secondary controls collapse into a persistent drawer
Prefer CSS Grid for desktop multi-column layouts with explicit grid-template-areas; switch to single-column flow with position:sticky for key controls at mobile breakpoints
For charts: use SVG-first rendering with canvas fallback for legacy browsers; keep simplified axis/legend in mobile to reduce paint cost
Tables: virtualize rows at >2000 rows and use progressive disclosure for column density; provide 'dense' toggle in UI
Modal behavior: global stacking context managed by JS (ordered z-index list) and CSS fallback with focus-trap polyfill for older Safari versions

2026-03-10 - Liam Patel: Updated prototype with container queries polyfill strategy and explicit scroll-lock approach for nested modals. Added focus-trap polyfill to prototype to validate keyboard flow.
Next steps: finalize handoff tokens, run accessibility pass with screen-reader testing, and coordinate engineering spike for Safari clipping fix (ENG-83890).
